text: dsh-session-batch-manager 是一个面向 DSH 网页客户端的会话管理插件。它通过 Cordis bundle 注册宿主路由与浏览器界面，在侧栏加入多选开关和操作工具条，并提供独立的会话管理面板。用户可以批量归档、恢复或删除会话，也能查看各会话的模型、token 用量、缓存读写和上下文压力。仪表盘支持筛选和树状会话展示，统计数据由宿主本地服务提供。适合需要集中整理会话并浏览会话用量信息的 DSH Web 用户。代码中未发现 API 密钥或外部服务配置要求。

dsh-session-batch-manager adds batch actions and a dashboard to DSH Web. Its bundle registers sidebar selection and host routes. Users can archive, restore, or delete sessions, then review model, token, cache, and context usage in a filterable panel. Stats use the local host service.
想在 DSH 侧栏里一次选中多条会话并批量归档或恢复。
我想查看每个会话的 token 消耗、缓存读写和上下文占用情况。
I want to remove several old sessions from the sidebar in one confirmed batch.
dsh-session-batch-manager 的功能「侧栏批量操作」：打开侧栏批量模式后可选择多条会话，并通过浮动工具条批量归档、恢复或删除；删除前会显示确认对话框，操作结果会汇总显示。
dsh-session-batch-manager 的功能「会话统计仪表盘」：从侧栏打开全屏面板后，可筛选会话并查看模型、token 用量、缓存读写和上下文压力；面板打开时定期更新统计，页面隐藏时暂停轮询。

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 0 Overview：Batch session management for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): multi-select sessions in the sidebar and batch **archive / unarchive / delete**, plus a full-screen **Session management** dashboard that visualizes **model, token usage, cache read/write, and context pressure** for every local session.

The DSH GUI natively offers per-session archiving only — there is no delete entry at all. This plugin fills the gap:
dsh-session-batch-manager README · 0 Overview：Verified with DSH 0.2.2-alpha.2 (Web UI, dev sandbox); see [6 Compatibility](#6-compatibility).

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 2.1 Sidebar batch management：- **Selection mode**: the **Batch** toggle at the bottom of the sidebar. Checkboxes are hidden by default and appear only in selection mode. While it is on, clicking anywhere on a row toggles its selection (opening, double-click rename, drag-sorting and Enter/Space are taken over). The selection survives leaving the mode — highlighted rows and the toolbar count stay; any batch operation (archive / unarchive / delete) clears it when it completes, and **Clear** clears it manually.
- **Floating toolbar** (bottom of the sidebar): appears whenever at least one session is selected, not only in selection mode. Shows the selected count, **Select all**, **Clear**, **Archive** (switches to **Unarchive** when every selected session is already archived), **Delete** (confirmation first) and **Exit** (selection mode only).
- **Stop-and-archive retry**: when batch archiving meets sessions with running work, they are reported separately and the result notice offers a one-click **Stop and archive N running sessions** retry — the same upgrade path as the native DSH archive dialog.
- **Batch delete**: the confirmation dialog lists the ta

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 2.2 Session management dashboard：A gauge-icon button at the bottom of the sidebar opens a full-screen, read-only **Session management** panel that scans every local session:

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 2.2 Session management dashboard：- **6-column table**: checkbox / session (title + running / subagent / archived / pinned badges + collapsible tree) / project / model (`provider/model`) / token usage (4-bucket total, per-bucket tooltip) / cache read · write / context pressure percentage (progress bar, warning color at ≥ 90%).
- **Two-pane filter**: **Main** (default, tree view with subagents nested under parent sessions) / **Archived** with live counts. Fork sessions are independent tree roots with full operation parity. Switching a pane clears the panel's selection set (independent from the sidebar's).
- **In-panel batch operations**: archive / unarchive / delete reuse the same core pipeline as the sidebar, with their own selection.
- **Progressive loading**: the first sweep is O(all logs) — skeleton rows first, then rows appended newest → oldest while the pending count decreases and a thin progress bar advances. Afterwards only sessions whose revision changed are replayed. The stats route responds immediately (fire-and-forget sweep) instead of blocking.

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 3 UI entry points：Both entries are buttons at the bottom of the DSH sidebar:

- **Batch** (checklist icon): toggles selection mode on the sidebar session list.
- **Session management** (gauge icon): opens / closes the full-screen dashboard panel.

While selection mode is on, the floating toolbar appears at the bottom of the sidebar as soon as at least one row is selected.
dsh-session-batch-manager README · 4 Installation：The repository ships prebuilt bundles under `lib/` (committed), so no build step is required to install.

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 4.1 Install from GitHub via CLI：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:mars401/dsh-session-batch-manager
```

Restart DSH Web after installation. If the browser still loads an older client bundle, use `Ctrl+Shift+R` to force-refresh the page.

Verify the installation:

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:<your-dsh-web-port>/dsh-session-batch-manager/v1/status

After changing plugin dependencies, `package.json`, or bundle configuration, reinstall the plugin or restart the corresponding client.

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 4.3 Configuration：| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `routeBase` | `/dsh-session-batch-manager/v1` | Host route prefix, injected into the page as `window.__DSH_SESSION_BATCH_MANAGER__` |
| `maxBatchSize` | `200` | Max session IDs per delete request |
| `trustedHosts` | `[]` | Additional trusted authorities for the host fence (only needed for non-loopback deployments) |
| `statsPollIntervalMs` | `5000` | Dashboard polling interval while the panel is open |
| `statsSweepConcurrency` | `4` | Cold-session observation concurrency |
dsh-session-batch-manager README · 5 Safety and behavior：Delete is evaluated **per session, independently** — one failure never affects the others. In order:

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 5 Safety and behavior：1. **Sessions with running work are refused** (`active`): in-progress turns, subagents, background tasks, timers — archive them first (archiving may stop tasks). Sessions that are merely mounted in memory but idle are allowed, matching native archive semantics (otherwise GUI-opened sessions could never be deleted before a restart).
2. **Physical deletion**: the JSONL log directory is located through the persistence layer (lazily materialized sessions are flushed first); the directory name must equal the encoded session ID and be truly contained in the persistence root (double validation against wrong deletions), then removed recursively.
3. **Registry accounting** (best-effort): live sessions go through an archive-set tombstone — hidden from the active view immediately, while still-open tabs are blocked by the native archived-session gate. Cold sessions are removed from the archive/pinned sets and detached from workspace records.
4. **Client-side tombstones**: successfully deleted IDs are persisted to the browser's `localStorage` and filtered from **all** views (including archived) across refreshes, so ghost rows of deleted l

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 5 Safety and behavior：**Browser trust fence** (mirrors DSH's `/api` trust model): the delete route only accepts POST requests carrying the plugin-specific `x-dsh-session-batch-manager` header; the Host must be a loopback spelling, the bound address, or listed in `trustedHosts`; `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` is a hard veto; the Origin must match; OPTIONS always answers 403 and no CORS headers are ever sent — a malicious web page cannot trigger a cross-site delete (the custom header forces a preflight, which is rejected). The stats route is read-only, sends `cache-control: no-store` and no CORS headers, and its payload carries no titles or secrets — only IDs, model names and token counts.

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 5 Safety and behavior：- Delete cleans the session log directory and registry accounting only; auxiliary state (KV entries, scheduled tasks, attachment caches) is out of scope for v0.1 — target sessions are already excluded from running state, so leftovers are lazy and harmless.
- Subagent sessions are excluded from the sidebar's **Select all** (matching the native list) but can be selected and deleted individually.
- Rows in search-result views don't render checkboxes (the host opens no row-action slot there); batch operations target the main list.
- The dashboard's context-percentage is an estimate (`contextPressure` is not an atomic observation) and may lag briefly after a model switch; the tooltip states this.
- Dashboard tooltips are plain text (the dsh Tooltip primitive supports string labels only); bucket breakdowns are newline-separated key-value pairs.

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 6 Compatibility：The plugin declares `dsh: ">=0.2.1"` in `engines`. **0.2.2-alpha.2** (dev sandbox, Web UI) has been fully verified end-to-end. **Desktop App 0.2.1-rc.5**: all seven coupling points (slots, services, events, `sessionQuery`) are present in the app bundle — static grep confirmation, runtime verification pending. Core features (batch archive/delete, sidebar checkboxes) use stable APIs available since 0.2.1. The session management dashboard stats use `sessionQuery`; on builds where this service is unavailable the panel degrades gracefully to list + batch operations (see `degraded` flag).

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 6 Compatibility：On DSH builds without a context-menu service, the context-menu entry is silently absent — see [2.1](#21-sidebar-batch-management).

This is a Cordis plugin with zero runtime dependencies: the host half is a plain ESM bundle, the client half is loaded through the DSH module loader.

dsh-session-batch-manager README · 7 Development：- `lib/host/index.js` is the host-side ESM plugin (delete route, stats route, index-inject config publication); `lib/client.js` is the client UI bundle. Both are committed so the repository installs without a build step; rebuild with `pnpm build` after source changes.
- Quality gates before submitting changes: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, `node --test tests/stats.test.mjs`.
- Source layout: `src/host/` (host half: routes, stats aggregator, trust fence, structured types), `src/client/` (browser half: batch ops, stores, dashboard panel and components), `tests/` (host unit tests), `docs/` (design / UI spec / review / test documents).
